name: Lucho Bermúdez
description:
'''Luis Eduardo Bermúdez Acosta''' (January 25 1912 – April 23 1994) better known as '''Lucho Bermúdez''', was a Colombian [[musician]], [[composer]], [[Arrangement|arranger]], director and [[Performing arts|performer]]. He is widely regarded as one of the most important fiugres in the 20th-century Colombian popular music. He adapted traditional Colombian musical genres such as [[Cumbia (Colombia)|cumbia]] and [[porro]] into orchestral arrangements that contributed to their emergence as symbols of Colombian national identity from the 1930s onwards.{{Citation needed|date=June 2020}}. 

Bermúdez's approach has often been described through the expressing "dressing porro in a tailcoat" ("Vestir el porro de ''frac''"), referring to his adaptation of a musical genre traditionally associated with working-class and rural communities into the sophisticated arrangements of big-band orchestras. By incorporating orchestral instrumentation and arrangementes associated with ballroom music, he helped bring porro to middle- and uper-class audiences and facilitated its wider circulation throughout Colombia. His work also gained recognition across [[Latin America]]. His compositions and arrangements drew heavily on the porros and [[Fandango|fandangos]] of the savanna region of [[Bolívar Department|Bolívar]]{{What|reason=|date=June 2020}} and the Caribbean [[Coast|coastal]] towns of northern Colombia. He also acknowledged the influence of musicians and composers such as [[Pedro Biava]], [[Ernesto Lecuona]] and [[Rafael Hernández Marín|Rafael Hernández]] on his work.
